conviction_note: Q3 2026 market conditions are public and favourable: Brent $97 against Eni's $85 guide deck, European refining markers roughly 2.5x Q2, TTF up. So a CFFO guide raise and an October extraordinary-dividend decision look likely, but 22 analysts and Eni's own published consensus (EBIT 5.69bn, refining 0.52bn) have already done this arithmetic. The stock is +9% over 20 days and +60% YTD at a record. Size is high for Eni (abs 4.0%, because a capital-return and guidance decision sits in the release; the Q2 guide raise moved +7.1%) and the sign is a slight lean (p_up 55). The findings sum (+1.0) is larger than the scaled number (+0.4) because the scaled number carries the sell-the-news risk that the findings do not net out.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 refining markers roughly 2.5x Q2: TotalEnergies ERM $33.2/b vs $13.5, BP RIM $46.7 vs $29.6, Shell ~$42 vs $24. Eni's own SERM ran only $9.1 in H1 against the $14 full-year deck. The SERM-linked extraordinary dividend Eni committed to decide in October (EUR0.08bn per $1 of SERM over the $6 budget) is therefore near-certain to activate, most likely at EUR0.6-1.0bn, above JPMorgan's EUR0.4bn and around Equita's EUR1bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 29 Jul 2026, guide and buyback raise with the extraordinary dividend flagged: +7.09% close-to-close (Yahoo bars). 24 Oct 2025, buyback raise at Q3: +1.6%.
findings.original_quote: nel mese di ottobre si deciderà sull'attivazione del dividendo straordinario, in linea con la politica di remunerazione comunicata al mercato che, in caso di scenari superiori a 90 $/bbl, o con un incremento superiore al 50% dei prezzi del gas o dei margini di raffinazione, prevede che il 100% dell'incremento del CFFO sia distribuito come dividendo straordinario nell'ultimo trimestre e sulla base delle sensitivity unitarie (1 $ SERM = €0,08 mld) [translation: in October the activation of the extraordinary dividend will be decided; under the policy, with a scenario above $90/bbl or a rise of more than 50% in gas prices or refining margins, 100% of the CFFO increase is paid as an extraordinary dividend in the last quarter, on the unit sensitivities ($1 SERM = EUR0.08bn)]
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is +9.1% over 20 days to a record. But the brokers' published amounts span EUR0.4-1.0bn, and Eni's SERM tracks the peer markers loosely (Q2 SERM 8.3 against ERM 13.5), so nobody knows the amount. If the market had settled on the high end, the gap between JPM and Equita would have closed and the targets would cluster. They do not: MS Hold EUR23.8 vs Barclays EUR32.

A fully priced raise would show as a consensus CFFO pre-WC above the 4.30bn Q3 figure, which is roughly what the deck implies and not more.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive on capital return and guidance while the priced lean (-0.456, run-up only) and the +9% 20-day run to a record lean against a further rise. The tension is why p_up sits at 55 and not higher.
language_note: Eni's Italian IR consensus page carries the full segment breakdown of the company-collected consensus (Refining 0.52, GGP 0.37, etc.); the English searches returned only conflicting Benzinga USD EPS figures.

The Italian Q2 release carries the exact October extraordinary-dividend mechanism ('nel mese di ottobre si deciderà sull'attivazione del dividendo straordinario ... (1 $ SERM = €0,08 mld)') and the H1 SERM of $9.1; English results searches did not surface either.

The Italian press (risparmioggi 19 Oct, money.it 6 Oct, soldionline 22 Oct) carried the broker range for the extraordinary dividend (Equita ~EUR1bn vs JPMorgan EUR400m) and the release timing 'prima dell'apertura di Piazza Affari'; nothing equivalent in English.
Peer scenario data (BP, Shell, TotalEnergies Q3 2026 indicators) came only from English sources.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 3.2 to 4.0, because the release likely carries a guidance change and a capital-return decision (Eni's own guide-raise print moved +7.09%), and reaction history was used for p_up rather than as a cap.
Guidance finding sized on the guidance scale: CFFO guide/buyback finding raised from +0.5 to +0.6.

'Positioning is the thing to beat, not to agree with' plus the truncated-zero rule: the run-up finding agrees with the priced lean, so it was cut from -0.6 to -0.4, and positioning_check states that no anchor exists.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': Q3 working capital added as an unknown line in new_in_release; there is no evidence to size it.
